node_definition.done_when: In a new tests/test_member_friction.py, against a synthesised temporary repository and a temporary configuration home (never the real roster, the real crew.json or the real pointer directory, and the test asserts the real pointer directory is untouched afterwards): a dispatch naming a registered member, run from inside the registered checkout without --repo, resolves the member instead of refusing; a dispatch from outside any checkout without --repo still refuses with a message naming --repo; and, for friction 2, a no-member dispatch from a session whose earlier review run's worker is still alive is admitted rather than refused member-in-flight. Record the base arm first: each case's outcome at base, and a case that already passes at base is reported as no longer reproducing rather than repaired. The named negative control (the checkout-derived repository removed from member resolution in reckon/crew/dispatch.py) is executed and fails the first case. Register no real roster member; a test fixture member lives only in the temporary configuration home. A peer's unpromoted run edits dispatch() to add a fence check, and another live node edits the routing call in dispatch; keep this change inside member resolution. The gate is the new test plus tests/test_crew_dispatch_arming.py and any existing test file whose name contains member, run at base and at head; list the files in the manifest. Each arm is recorded as JSON carrying completed true and a literal command with absolute paths and no angle-bracket placeholder; each log names its revision on the first line and ends with a bare line reading EXIT= followed by the exit code. Every pytest process uses a basetemp private to that process. The head arm adds no failure id; any added id means status blocked, naming each id. ruff check and ruff format --check over the changed Python paths report no finding the base did not. Scratch goes under /tmp in a directory named for this run and is deleted before status complete. An evidence fragment at docs/evidence/fragments/new-work-gets-a-new-worker/member-friction.html records which friction reproduced and what changed. The turn ends once the manifest reads complete or blocked.
node_definition.goal: Close followup f-nwgnw-member-friction of new-work-gets-a-new-worker: reproduce each of its two frictions at base in a synthesised temporary repository, repair the one that still reproduces, and report the other with the evidence that it no longer does. Friction 1: crew dispatch with --member naming a registered member refuses that the member cannot be resolved without a repository even when run from the registered checkout, until --repo is passed; the repair resolves the repository from the working checkout the same way a no-member dispatch does. Friction 2: a finished review whose worker process is still alive holds the session member, so a later no-member dispatch from the same session is refused member-in-flight; check whether no-member dispatches now run under their own disposable identity so this no longer reproduces.
